I checked the solution step by step and found no errors.

- **Factorization:** Expanding $(x^2+10x-36)^2 + (x+27)^2$ gives $x^4+20x^3+28x^2-720x+1296 + x^2+54x+729 = x^4+20x^3+29x^2-666x+2025$, which equals $P(x)$.
- **Quadratic factors:** Setting $x^2+10x-36 = i(x+27)$ gives $x^2+(10-i)x-36-27i=0$. The discriminant is $(10-i)^2+4(36+27i) = 99-20i+144+108i = 243+88i$, so $x=\frac{-10+i\pm\sqrt{243+88i}}{2}$.
- **Which root is in the first quadrant:** Here $|243+88i|=\sqrt{66793}\approx 258.45$. So the principal root $p+qi$ has $p^2\approx 250.7$, giving $p\approx 15.83$, and $q=44/p\approx 2.78$. The "+" root has real part $(−10+15.83)/2>0$ and imaginary part $(1+2.78)/2>0$.
- **Uniqueness:** The "−" root has negative real part. The case-2 roots are the conjugates of the case-1 roots. The conjugate of the "+" root has negative imaginary part, and the conjugate of the "−" root has negative real part. So the first-quadrant root is unique.

This gives $a=-10,\ b=1,\ c=243,\ d=88$, so $a+b+c+d=322$.
